$\underset{\sim}{t}$ steps $1$ across and $2$ up, so both its length and its direction differ.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{u}$ steps $4$ across and $1$ up.
$\underset{\sim}{v}$ steps $4$ across and $1$ up as well, so it has the same magnitude and direction.
$\underset{\sim}{v}$ is equal to $\underset{\sim}{u}$, even though it is drawn higher up the grid.

$\underset{\sim}{k}$ points back the other way but steps $2$ left and $2$ down, so its magnitude does not match.

questions.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{g}$ steps $3$ across and $2$ up, so its negative must step $3$ left and $2$ down.
$\underset{\sim}{h}$ steps $3$ left and $2$ down, giving the same length and the opposite direction.
$\underset{\sim}{h}$ is the negative of $\underset{\sim}{g}$.

questions.question_text:
Two arrows on a grid are both $4$ units long and both point due east.
One starts at $(0,0)$ and the other starts at $(2,5)$.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: They are equal vectors, because they have the same magnitude and the same direction.
They are not equal, because they start at different points.
options.why: Where an arrow is drawn is not part of the vector; only its magnitude and direction count.

options.text: They are negatives of each other, because they are drawn in different places.
options.why: Negatives must point in opposite directions, and both of these arrows point due east.

options.text: They are equal only if they are drawn from the same point.
options.why: Treats the starting point as part of the vector; one vector has many directed line segments.

questions.solution_text:
Both arrows are $4$ units long, so the magnitudes match.
Both point due east, so the directions match.
The starting point is not part of a vector, so the two vectors are equal.

questions.question_text:
$\overrightarrow{AB}$ takes you $2$ units left and $6$ units up.
$C$ is the point $(4,-3)$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}=\overrightarrow{AB}$.
What are the coordinates of $D$?

options.why: Added $2$ to the $x$-coordinate; a step to the left subtracts from $x$.
Subtracted $6$ from the $y$-coordinate; a step up adds to $y$.
Moved right instead of left and down instead of up, reversing the whole step.

questions.solution_text:
An equal vector makes the same step, so $\overrightarrow{CD}$ goes $2$ left and $6$ up from $C$.
$(4-2,\ -3+6)$
$=(2,3)$

questions.question_text:
$A$ is $(0,1)$ and $B$ is $(3,5)$; $C$ is $(2,-2)$ and $D$ is $(5,2)$; $E$ is $(1,1)$ and $F$ is $(5,4)$.
Which pair of vectors is equal?

options.why: Both steps use the numbers $3$ and $4$, but $\overrightarrow{EF}$ goes $4$ across and $3$ up, so the directions differ.
Compared the endpoint coordinates instead of the step from each tail to its head.

questions.solution_text:
From $A$ to $B$ the step is $3-0=3$ across and $5-1=4$ up.
From $C$ to $D$ the step is $5-2=3$ across and $2-(-2)=4$ up.
From $E$ to $F$ the step is $5-1=4$ across and $4-1=3$ up.
$\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ make the same step, so they are the equal pair.

questions.question_text:
$\overrightarrow{KL}$ has magnitude $6$ cm on a bearing of $065^{\circ}$.
Which of these describes $\overrightarrow{LK}$?

options.why: Reversed the letters but left the direction unchanged; $\overrightarrow{LK}$ points the opposite way.
Subtracted the bearing from $180^{\circ}$ instead of adding $180^{\circ}$ to reverse it.
Made the magnitude negative instead of reversing the direction; a magnitude is a length and is never negative.

questions.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{LK}$ runs along the same segment the other way, so its magnitude is still $6$ cm.
$065^{\circ}+180^{\circ}$
$=245^{\circ}$
$\overrightarrow{LK}$ is $6$ cm on a bearing of $245^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text:
Two arrows are the same length and lie along parallel lines, but they point in opposite directions.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Each vector is the negative of the other.

options.why: Equal vectors must point the same way; lying along parallel lines is not enough.

options.text: The magnitudes of the two vectors are negatives of each other.
options.why: The minus sign reverses the direction, not the length; both magnitudes are the same positive number.
Equal length with opposite direction is exactly the negative relationship.

questions.solution_text:
The two arrows have the same length, so the magnitudes match.
They point opposite ways, so the directions are reversed.
Same magnitude with opposite direction means each vector is the negative of the other.

questions.question_text:
$\underset{\sim}{a}$ takes you $8$ units right and $6$ units up.
Which of these vectors is equal to $\underset{\sim}{a}$?

options.why: This steps $8$ left and $6$ down, so it is the negative of $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
This steps $6$ across and $8$ up, swapping the across and up parts of the step.
This points the same way but is only half as long, so it is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{a}$ rather than equal to it.

questions.solution_text:
From $(-5,-1)$ to $(3,5)$ the step is $3-(-5)=8$ across and $5-(-1)=6$ up.
That is the same step as $\underset{\sim}{a}$, so the magnitude and direction both match.
The vector from $(-5,-1)$ to $(3,5)$ is equal to $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
